# The published prior-predictive intervals, restricted to draws the model calls viable

*Generated by `scripts/intervals_under_admissibility.py`. The per-draw measurements need the compiled Python extension and are committed; every figure here is derived from that file, so CI re-derives the page and runs no simulation.*

## What was never checked

`uncertainty-intervals-report.md` publishes 95% prior-predictive intervals over uniform priors across 11 PRCC rate-constant ranges, 2000 joint draws at 2000 cells each. The manuscript separately states that every phenotype must show less than 2% death under Control, and `headline_at_fitted.py` already uses that constraint to reject the in-vitro-fitted cascade.

**The published design evaluates treated arms only.** Its 8 conditions contain no Control arm, so the untreated death rate was never computed and a draw's admissibility was not knowable from the artifact. This page adds the 3 untreated arms on the SAME draws -- one sample partitioned, not two sampled, so the conditioning is not confounded with sampling noise.

## How much of the prior is admissible

**754 of 2000 draws (37.7%).** Across the whole prior the worst untreated death rate has median 4.1%, 90th percentile 47.4% and maximum 96.5%; 179 draws kill more than half the untreated population.

## One mechanism, two opposite-looking corrections

Admissibility keeps the draws whose defences are strong enough that an untreated cell survives, so it lowers kill everywhere. That shows up as two different-looking effects, and reporting either alone would flatter whichever was looked at first.

**The inducer arms' upper tails collapse** (2 of 8 conditions): PersisterNrf2/RSL3, OXPHOS/RSL3. The published intervals say those phenotypes COULD be killed much harder than the admissible model allows, and the draws that achieve it are ones where the untreated cell is already dead.

**The exogenous-ROS arms' lower tails extend further down** (3 of 8): PersisterNrf2/SDT, Glycolytic/SDT, OXPHOS/SDT. Here the published intervals are too OPTIMISTIC at the bottom, which is the opposite direction and the same cause.

**And 2 are unmoved**: Persister/SDT, Glycolytic/RSL3. A condition pinned at a floor or a ceiling across the whole prior has nowhere to go, which is why this is reported per condition rather than as one verdict.

Verdict: `conditioning_changes_what_the_intervals_say`.

## Which of the published conclusions survive

Each is quoted from the committed report and scored on the property it actually rests on, because several rest on different properties of the same table and one verdict would hide the ones that fail. A guard asserts every quoted fragment is still in that report, so a rewrite there forces a rewrite here.

| published conclusion | survives | on what basis |
|---|---|---|
| "The RSL3 death rates carry the widest intervals" | **no** | full prior: Persister/RSL3 widest at 0.981, next 0.965 (margin 0.015); admissible: Glycolytic/SDT widest at 0.992, next 0.887 |
| "OXPHOS x RSL3 stays low-but-wide" | **no** | admissible width 0.068 against a 0.25 bar (was 0.751) |
| "The Glycolytic x RSL3 floor (~0% across the entire prior) is the robust exception" | **yes** | admissible upper end 0.0000 |
| "Persister x SDT sits >98% across the entire prior" | **no** | admissible lower end 0.9634 against the 0.98 the claim quotes about itself |
| "the Glycolytic x SDT interval is WIDE" | **yes** | admissible width 0.992 against a 0.25 bar (was 0.965) |

**3 of 5 refuted, 2 survive.**

The one that matters most is the report's LEAD interpretation. It says the inducer rates are the least constrained, and under the model's own viability constraint the least-constrained condition is an exogenous-ROS one instead. The basis column shows that claim was true by a thin margin on the full prior rather than comfortably, which is the honest way to describe a reversal: not that it was badly wrong, but that it was never far from flipping and the constraint flips it.

## What this does NOT establish

**Conditioning is not inference.** Removing draws the model itself declares invalid adds no data. It cannot turn a prior-predictive interval into a data-conditioned one, and `identifiability-report.json`'s data-conditioned-headline count is unchanged by everything on this page.

**The admissible subset is not a posterior either.** It is the same uniform prior with a region removed, so its median is a property of the box that remains, not an estimate of anything. The 37.7% figure describes the prior's overlap with a viability constraint and nothing else.

**The constraint is a modelling choice, stated in prose.** It is imported from the generator whose guard parses it out of the manuscript, so if the manuscript's number changes this page follows; but nothing here measures whether under-that-percentage untreated death is the right bar.

**The spatial and combination headline intervals are NOT corrected here.** `headline-uncertainty-report.md` and its `-tme-` and `-penetration-` siblings sweep the same prior through compiled binaries at minutes per run, so recomputing them conditioned was not attempted. The admissible fraction above is the size of the correction they need, and it is outstanding rather than applied -- saying so is the point, because silently leaving them beside a corrected page would imply they had been checked.

**Admissibility is judged on 3 phenotypes, not all of them.** The same three `headline_at_fitted` uses, so the two pages judge it identically. Measured separately, adding the remaining phenotypes changes no verdict because Persister always binds, so the subset is not a weakening -- but it is a subset, and the fraction above is therefore an upper bound on admissibility.
